core.inventory.name: core.inventory
core.inventory.status: ported complete (all pure-compute modules incl. python-ast call_graph + extractor, 197 cargo tests; builder.py filesystem walk/cache stays Python-side by design, same as reach_cache load_index/save_index)
core.inventory.notes: Ported (oracle-verified): build_membership, coverage, diff, exclusions, fixture_detection, languages, lookup, reach_witness, dead_scope, module_load_abort, translation_view, extractors (tree-sitter core + Python-ast fallback), call_graph (all languages incl. Python ast-based), builder.process_file_content + call_graph_for (incl. python). PARTIAL: reach_cache (compute_fingerprint + is_valid_fingerprint ported & byte-verified; load_index/save_index NOT ported — they pickle reachability._AdjacencyIndex, left Python-side by design). PYTHON-AST GAP CLOSED (2026-06-30): extract_call_graph_python (+_PythonCallGraph walker, _decorator_chain/_attribute_chain) ported to call_graph.rs; PythonExtractor (ast-based function extraction with ast.unparse-equivalent signature formatting) ported to ts_extract.rs and wired into extract_items's zero-function fallback exactly as the Python orchestration does. New deps: rustpython-parser/rustpython-ast 0.4 (CPython-ast-shaped parse tree) + rustpython-unparser 0.2 (used narrowly; a hand-rolled CPython-faithful unparser subset (py_unparse) replaces it for subscript/generic annotations where the crate's output diverges from ast.unparse, e.g. Dict[str, int] vs Dict[(str, int)]). 26 new oracle-differential tests (171->197), each transcribed from the live Python ast/extractors oracle; independently spot-verified against a fresh live-Python run on a separate fixture (not in the test suite) covering nested-function-in-if/try/with, decorator-scope, self/cls receiver_class, getattr/importlib/__import__ indirection, relative + wildcard imports, and ast.unparse generics (Optional/Dict/Callable/Tuple/PEP604 unions) — byte-exact match. REMAINING GAP (intentionally Python-side, not pure-compute): builder.py's filesystem walk + orchestration (build_inventory, _collect_source_files, _count_source_files, default_cache_dir, _carry_forward_coverage) and the stat+sha256 incremental-rebuild cache — these are I/O/threading concerns naturally left on the Python side of the PyO3 boundary (Python walks + caches, calls Rust per file), consistent with reach_cache's load_index/save_index being left Python-side for the same reason. core.build.macro_config + core.build.rust_modules build-membership gates are outside core.inventory. reach_audit depends on reachability (done).
